h1: The 8 Best Monitors Under $300 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best monitors under $300, including QHD gaming panels, USB-C single-cable models, and a 4K office pick, compared on specs.
summary: The ASUS TUF Gaming VG27AQ3A is our top pick, with a 27 inch QHD Fast IPS panel at 180Hz in the sub-$200 tier. The Dell S2725DSM is the cheapest QHD option, the Dell S2725DC is the single-cable USB-C pick, and the Philips 27E1N5900R is the 4K choice for office work. The LG 27G640A tops out at 300Hz for fast-paced gamers.
intro: Under $300 you can now buy a QHD monitor with a fast refresh rate, which makes the old trade between sharp and fast mostly obsolete. The real decision is what you do with it: gaming wants refresh rate, laptop users want USB-C power delivery, and spreadsheet work wants pixel density.

We reviewed eight monitors on paper, comparing resolution, refresh rate, panel type, and connectivity from the spec sheets. Models in the upper price tier should be checked against the live price before you buy, since we only know their bracket.

products.name: ASUS TUF Gaming VG27AQ3A 27-Inch QHD 180Hz
products.verdict: QHD at 180Hz with the broadest adaptive sync support.
products.description:
The VG27AQ3A is a 27 inch QHD Fast IPS panel running at 180Hz with a 1ms response time. It supports ELMB Sync, G-Sync compatibility, and FreeSync Premium, covers 130% sRGB, supports HDR10, and has built-in speakers. It sits in the $100 to $200 tier.

It leads because it delivers the best gaming performance per dollar, with sync support that covers both major graphics card brands. The LG goes faster at 300Hz but costs more.

Buy it if you play games and also work on the same screen. The caveat is that it has no USB-C input listed.
products.idealFor: Gamers who also use the monitor for work.
products.skipIf: You want a single-cable laptop dock.

products.name: Dell 27 Plus QHD Monitor S2725DSM
products.verdict: QHD at 144Hz at the lowest price in the group.
products.description:
The S2725DSM is a 27 inch QHD IPS monitor at 144Hz with 1ms MPRT, a 1500:1 contrast ratio, and a 4-star TUV eye comfort rating. It has dual 3W speakers and AMD FreeSync, and it sits in the $100 to $200 tier.

It costs less than the ASUS and gives up 36Hz of refresh and the broader sync coverage. For office use and casual gaming, the difference is small.

Choose it for the cheapest route to QHD. The caveat is the lower refresh rate.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want QHD sharpness.
products.skipIf: You use an Nvidia card and want G-Sync.

products.name: Dell 27 Plus QHD USB-C Monitor S2725DC
products.verdict: A real single-cable setup with 65W power delivery.
products.description:
The S2725DC is a 27 inch QHD IPS at 144Hz with 1ms MPRT. It adds USB-C with 65W power delivery for a single-cable setup, plus a small pop-up port panel for quick plug-ins. It sits in the upper price tier of this guide.

The 65W delivery is enough to charge most thin laptops while sending video, which is the reason it beats the S2725DSM for laptop users.

Buy it if you work from a USB-C laptop. The caveat is that it costs more than the plain Dell.
products.idealFor: Laptop users who want one cable.

products.name: Philips 27" 4K UHD USB-C Monitor 27E1N5900R
products.verdict: 4K sharpness and USB-C docking over gaming speed.
products.description:
The Philips 27E1N5900R is a 27 inch 4K UHD IPS panel at 3840 by 2160 with USB-C 65W power delivery, a USB 3.2 hub, DisplayHDR 400, and a 4-year advance replacement warranty. It sits in the upper price tier.

It ranks below the Dell USB-C because the refresh rate is not listed, which hints at an office-first design. In return you get 4K text clarity and the longest warranty in the guide.

Choose it for documents, photos, and docking. The caveat is that it is not aimed at gamers.
products.idealFor: Office work and photo editing with a laptop.
products.skipIf: You want a fast gaming panel.

products.name: LG 27G640A-B UltraGear 27-Inch QHD 300Hz
products.verdict: The fastest refresh rate here, at 300Hz.
products.description:
The UltraGear 27G640A-B is a 27 inch QHD IPS monitor at 300Hz with 1ms response. It supports VESA DisplayHDR 400, covers 95% DCI-P3, and offers USB-C with 15W power delivery, dual HDMI 2.1, and DisplayPort 1.4. It sits in the upper price tier.

It places lower in our ranking because 300Hz only pays off with a very strong graphics card, and the 15W USB-C cannot charge a laptop. For competitive players it is the pick.

Buy it if frame rate is your priority. The caveat is that you need a powerful PC to use the speed.
products.skipIf: You do not have a high-end graphics card.

products.name: Samsung 32" Odyssey G5 (G50F) QHD Gaming Monitor
products.verdict: The largest QHD screen here, at 32 inches.
products.description:
The Odyssey G5 G50F is a 32 inch QHD Fast IPS display at 180Hz with 1ms GtG, HDR10, G-Sync compatibility, and AMD FreeSync. It adds Black Equalizer and Virtual Aim Point gaming aids and sits in the upper price tier.

Compared with the 27 inch ASUS it offers more screen at the same resolution, which makes pixels larger and slightly less sharp. It is a good fit if you sit farther back.

Choose it for a bigger display. The caveat is lower pixel density.
products.idealFor: Gamers who want a big screen.

products.name: LG 32G600A-B UltraGear 32-Inch Curved QHD
products.description:
The LG 32G600A-B is a 32 inch curved IPS QHD display with a 1000R curve, 180Hz, 1ms, HDR10, up to 99% sRGB, AMD FreeSync, and a three-side virtually borderless design. It sits in the upper price tier.

The curve is the draw, wrapping the image around your view, though it can warp straight lines for design work. Samsung's flat 32 inch offers broader sync.

Buy it for immersive games. The caveat is distortion for precise layout tasks.
products.skipIf: You do design or CAD work.

products.name: ASUS VA27AQ 27-Inch QHD IPS
products.verdict: QHD sharpness for work at only 75Hz.
products.description:
The ASUS VA27AQ is a 27 inch QHD IPS monitor at 75Hz with 1ms response, 99% sRGB, and a frameless VESA-ready design. Inputs include HDMI, DisplayPort, and VGA, plus built-in speakers. It sits in the $100 to $200 tier.

It lands last since 75Hz is slow next to the 144Hz Dell at a similar tier, but it is the only one with VGA, helpful for older equipment.

Choose it for spreadsheets and documents. The caveat is the refresh rate.

whatMatters.detail: QHD is 2560 by 1440 and 4K is 3840 by 2160. Higher resolution gives sharper text on the same size. Check the pixel count in the title or specs.
Refresh is how many times the screen updates per second. 144Hz and above feels smoother for games, while 75Hz is fine for office work. Check the Hz figure in the bullets.
USB-C PD lets one cable carry video and charge a laptop. 65W suits thin laptops, while 15W only trickles. Check the wattage in the listing.
G-Sync and FreeSync reduce tearing. Nvidia cards work best with G-Sync compatible displays. Check which are listed.
A 32 inch screen needs more desk depth, and a curve suits immersion but can distort straight lines. Match size to your viewing distance.

cards.text: You dock a laptop or need 4K, where the Dell S2725DC or Philips earn their price.

faq.q: Will my laptop charge over USB-C?
faq.a: Only if the monitor delivers enough watts. The Dell S2725DC and Philips offer 65W, while the LG 27G640A offers 15W.
Paying for 300Hz without a graphics card to match.
At 27 inches, yes. Text and images are noticeably sharper.

faq.q: How do I set refresh rate?
faq.a: Set it in your operating system display settings and use DisplayPort or HDMI 2.1 for high rates.
The ASUS VA27AQ lists a VESA design. Check the listing for others.
HDR400 modes help little compared with true HDR displays, so don't pay extra for it alone.

finalTake: The ASUS TUF Gaming VG27AQ3A is the best all-round monitor on this list, giving QHD at 180Hz with broad sync support. Pick the Dell S2725DC if you dock a laptop and the Philips if you want 4K. Confirm the live price on the upper-tier models against your $300 limit before buying.
